You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE museum (
    Museum_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Num_of_Staff INT,
    Open_Year TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Museum_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE visitor (
    ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Level_of_membership INT,
    Age INT,
    UNIQUE (ID)
);

CREATE TABLE visit (
    Museum_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    visitor_ID TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Num_of_Ticket INT,
    Total_spent REAL,
    PRIMARY KEY (Museum_ID, visitor_ID),
    UNIQUE (Museum_ID, visitor_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (visitor_ID) REFERENCES visitor(ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Museum_ID) REFERENCES museum(Museum_ID)
);

What do you mean by “rich visitor”? Here are a few common interpretations—pick one and I’ll tailor the query:

### 1) Visitors who spent the most total money (overall)
```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  v.Level_of_membership,
  v.Age,
  SUM(vi.Total_spent) AS total_spent
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name, v.Level_of_membership, v.Age
ORDER BY total_spent DESC;
```

### 2) “Richest” = top N spenders (e.g., top 10)
```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  v.Level_of_membership,
  v.Age,
  SUM(vi.Total_spent) AS total_spent
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name, v.Level_of_membership, v.Age
ORDER BY total_spent DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

### 3) Visitors who spent more than a threshold (e.g., > 1000)
```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  v.Level_of_membership,
  v.Age,
  SUM(vi.Total_spent) AS total_spent
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name, v.Level_of_membership, v.Age
HAVING SUM(vi.Total_spent) > 1000
ORDER BY total_spent DESC;
```

Tell me which definition you want (top spender, top N, threshold, or per museum), and if you want the output to include which museums they visited.
just give me details on the visitor who bought the most tickets

```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  v.Level_of_membership,
  v.Age,
  SUM(vi.Num_of_Ticket) AS total_tickets
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name, v.Level_of_membership, v.Age
ORDER BY total_tickets DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
the visitor's name should be included in the details

```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name AS visitor_name,
  v.Level_of_membership,
  v.Age,
  SUM(vi.Num_of_Ticket) AS total_tickets
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name, v.Level_of_membership, v.Age
ORDER BY total_tickets DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
the ticket purchase should be from a single transaction

```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name AS visitor_name,
  v.Level_of_membership,
  v.Age,
  vi.Museum_ID,
  vi.Num_of_Ticket,
  vi.Total_spent
FROM visit vi
JOIN visitor v ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
ORDER BY vi.Num_of_Ticket DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
also need the visitor's age along with the name

```sql
SELECT
  v.Name AS visitor_name,
  v.Age,
  vi.Museum_ID,
  vi.Num_of_Ticket,
  vi.Total_spent
FROM visit vi
JOIN visitor v ON v.ID = vi.visitor_ID
ORDER BY vi.Num_of_Ticket DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
